output.answer: The wide (±40%) cbBTC/WETH position was rejected on Aerodrome (E8.4, closed 8 Sep 2026) because Aerodrome's gauge mechanics concentrate rewards in a tiny band: a staked position earns only AERO emissions (no fees — fees go to voters), and the displayed Emission APR is emissions divided by liquidity staked in the active tick ±1 tick (a ~0.3% band on the CL10 pool). The project's ±40% range has liquidity-per-dollar ≈6.5 versus ≈1,300 for that band — a ~0.5% share, worth only ≈4–6%/yr in AERO (CL100: ~3.8%/yr). On Uniswap the same ±40% position earns ≈5–11%/yr in fees (pool-wide 24–58% × ~0.19 wide-leg coefficient), with no token to sell (AERO has 10.9%/yr inflation plus FX risk). Aerodrome's edge exists only for ultra-narrow, actively managed positions — the 'narrowing/chasing price' class the project had already falsified on 26–31 Aug. Verdict: no, without code and without capital; Uniswap remains the best venue for wide LP on this pair, and the question was closed permanently (like WETH/USDC on 2 Sep).

output.answer: On 17 August 2026 the project hit a .bot/pipeline incident on the Windows server. The core risk: the live .bot/ directory had been force-added to git while the auto-pull runner performed a `git reset --hard` every 3 minutes, so it would overwrite live bot data (state, logs, proposals) with the repo version. Fable detected the risk; CC-Win then (step 0) made a robocopy backup and stopped the runner, and diagnosed the HomosPipeline failure (a SYSTEM task failing with `spawn npx ENOENT`, the third iteration of the lesson that node/npm/git on that Windows box must run as the elo account). CC-Mac held the untrack until step 0 was confirmed (a confirmation deadlock Fable cut through by having CC-Win record the confirmation locally without pushing). Then the .bot files were untracked (commit f18f50e), CC-Win pulled, restored the backup, re-ran the pipeline as elo with a manual fetch:llama, restarted the runner and the bot. Result: zero data loss. Separately, the pipeline (07:30 schtask) had apparently been broken since 10.08 (no pipeline.log, DefiLlama data 158h stale, selector refusing on stale data for 5 days); it was re-pointed to the elo account. A 48h TTL was added to OPEN/ROTATE proposals. The next day (18 Aug) the auto-pull runner was withdrawn entirely — code now reaches the server only by manual `git pull` — because the every-3-minute `reset --hard` was the risk class behind the incident.

output.answer: The package was pinned to exactly 1.0.0 (no caret) on 2026-08-19 because Envio stopped shipping the win32 native binary after 1.0.0. The caret range (^1.4.0) resolved on Windows to a wrapper without the native module, causing a hard throw before the RPC fallback, while on macOS the same version worked (darwin binaries go up to 1.4.0). The API the project uses is identical in 1.0.0 (verified by diff), and the pin was independently confirmed in the npm registry. A local test on Windows with 1.0.0 produced the first fully clean fetch run (18/18 pools exit 0). The team preferred a shared lockfile over the unused 1.x helpers.

output.answer: On 2 September 2026 the tranche exit rule was set as: exit the LP on 24 September regardless of price, or earlier if the tranche balance reaches +5% (≥ $6 396.60 on the $6 092 deposit); capital would go to the exchange and then to ETFs, with manual daily monitoring and deliberately no automation. The 16 September revision (made the day after a −4% move) changed this to: exit the LP when the tranche balance is at or above the deposit (0%, i.e. ≥ $6 092); the hard 24 September exit and the +5% trigger were both dropped; 24 September became a review rather than an exit date; a balance at or below −10% (~$5 480) would force a new exit decision; a bet review was set for 24 October; and no narrowing (FLAT_NARROW) would still be signed. The rationale was that the loss was entirely ETH/BTC market beta (−$12 vs HODL), and the owner kept a conscious bet on an ETH/BTC recovery while refusing to exit below the deposit.

output.answer: ALGORITHM v1, frozen on 11 August 2026, specified: pool selection (7-day window + 3-day persistence + majors); a rebalancing range of k·σ with k = 3 for ETH/stable and k = 2 for cbBTC; a rebalance trigger with 24 h hysteresis and payback ≤ 7 days; a trend breaker that is a plain exit when price breaks 5% below the 7-day EMA (half-life 7 days); fee collection at 8× gas; and a portfolio of WETH/USDC 0.3% Base (active) plus cbBTC/WETH 0.05% Base (active, k=2), with mainnet passive ±50% only. Evidence: a 365-day walk-forward plus 5 out-of-sample cross-validation runs. The plain-exit trend profile was chosen because it was the best outside the tuning pool and had the fewest parameters; on the out-of-sample pools (cbBTC, base-005, mainnet-005) plain exit beat or tied the re>EMA variant (cbBTC +0.88 vs +0.61). The same day, revision v1.1 changed the re-entry rule for ETH/stable to 'price back above EMA' after full 365-day runs on two pools (22 windows each) reversed the morning ranking from 4-window 90-day runs, with the first full gate pass on base-005 (68% win rate, worst window −2.52%).

output.answer: Ran the 30-day walk-forward on Base WETH/USDC 0.05% (365d history, 10-day step, 34 windows: 6 up, 12 down, 16 flat). Passive ±50% ("Pasywny ±50%") versus HODL 50/50 per 30-day window: mean -0.35%, median +0.99%, win rate 67.6% (23 of 34 windows positive), worst window -14.78%, best +3.01%. Its own APR quartiles: Q25 -73.6%, median +12.8%, Q75 +78.7%. By regime: up windows (6) mean +0.31%, 83% win rate; down windows (12) mean -3.61%, only 17% win rate, worst -14.78%; flat windows (16) mean +1.86%, 100% win rate. Over the last 90 days (6 windows) it was slightly negative: mean -0.40%, 50% win rate. It meets the script's win-rate criterion (≥65%) but not its worst-window gate (worst > -3%), since -14.78% fails.

A live 720-day walk-forward can't be run (the allowlist caps windowDays at 180), but a saved result with exactly these settings exists: walkforward-base-cbbtc-weth-005-720d-30d (720-day history, 30-day windows, 15-day step, 47 windows). Passive ±50% vs HODL 50/50: overall mean -0.30%, median +0.20%, win rate 63.8%, worst window -7.76%, best +1.30%; own-APR quartiles Q25 -69.7%, median 56.4%, Q75 201.0%. By regime: Up (5 windows) mean -4.51%, win rate 0%; Down (12) mean -0.47%, win rate 33.3%; Flat (30) mean +0.47%, win rate 86.7%. Recent 90 days: 4 windows, all positive (100% win rate), mean +0.13%. Verdict: it is essentially a flat-market strategy — it wins decisively when the pair is rangebound but loses to HODL in up moves and mostly down moves. It misses the project's 'sound' bar (win rate 63.8% < 65%, worst -7.76% < -3) and wins in only 1 of 3 regimes (flat), so it fails the gate of beating HODL in at least 2 regimes. Note: this is a saved file, not a fresh run, so it may reflect an older engine version.
